actions.title: Replace the upper-tail reduction with absolute moments.
actions.summary: Ask for a uniform even-moment estimate. It suffices for the two-sided theorem by applying Markov to |Q|ᵖ and choosing p at the tail scale.
actions.math:
Sufficient goal: ‖Q‖p ≤ C₀K²(√p F + p O) for every even p ≥ 2.
ℙ(|Q| ≥ t) ≤ t⁻ᵖ 𝔼|Q|ᵖ. The final steps choose p and handle small q.
actions.check: This is an open obligation, not an established moment estimate. No upper-tail result for Q or −Q is invoked.
actions.tool: Markov inequality for a nonnegative random variable.
actions.observation: Absolute moments encode both signs at once.

actions.title: Expand the centered quadratic form.
actions.summary: Separate independent squares from cross terms.
actions.math:
Q = D + S.
D = Σᵢ aᵢᵢ(Xᵢ² − 𝔼Xᵢ²); S = Σᵢ≠ⱼ aᵢⱼXᵢXⱼ.
actions.check: Independence and zero means give 𝔼XiXj = 0 for i ≠ j. No symmetry of A is required.
actions.observation: The same algebraic split remains useful after removing the sign strategy.

actions.title: Reduce to two moment bounds by Minkowski.
actions.summary: The diagonal and off-diagonal moment estimates together suffice for the requested estimate of Q.
actions.math:
‖D + S‖p ≤ ‖D‖p + ‖S‖p.
Require both ‖D‖p and ‖S‖p ≤ CK²(√p F + p O), uniformly over even p ≥ 2.
actions.check: Minkowski applies for p ≥ 1; D and S need not be independent. Both branches still need proofs.
actions.observation: Splitting a norm avoids splitting the tail event.

actions.title: Expand even powers of the diagonal sum.
actions.summary: Prove diagonal moment control directly, so a quoted tail inequality cannot conceal the excluded strategy.
actions.math:
Zi = aᵢᵢ(Xᵢ² − 𝔼Xᵢ²); choose Mi = CK²|aᵢᵢ| with 𝔼|Zi|ᵏ ≤ k! Miᵏ (k ≥ 2).
σ² = ΣMi², b = max Mi. Centering eliminates exponents 1.
𝔼|ΣZi|²ᵐ/(2m)! ≤ [z²ᵐ] ∏ᵢ(1 + Σₖ≥₂ Miᵏzᵏ)
≤ [z²ᵐ] exp(σ²z²/(1 − bz)).
actions.check: Independence factors mixed moments. Bound their absolute values termwise; Miᵏ ≤ Mi²bᵏ⁻². The formal power series majorant is coefficientwise nonnegative. Its exponential is not a random quadratic-form MGF.
actions.tool: Subgaussian-square and centered subexponential moment bounds; multinomial expansion; coefficientwise majorization.
actions.observation: For even powers, the whole moment is nonnegative; centering removes singleton factors.

actions.title: Choose a radius and close the diagonal moment goal.
actions.summary: Evaluate the nonnegative coefficient majorant at a suitable radius.
actions.math:
For p = 2m, r = min{√m/(2σ), 1/(2b)}.
[z²ᵐ] exp(σ²z²/(1 − bz)) ≤ r⁻²ᵐ exp(σ²r²/(1 − br)).
σ²r²/(1 − br) ≤ m/2; ((2m)!)¹ᐟ²ᵐ ≤ 2m.
‖D‖₂ₘ ≤ C(√m σ + mb) ≤ CK²(√p F + p O).
actions.check: If b = 0 all diagonal coefficients vanish and D = 0. Otherwise 0 < r < 1/b. Use σ ≤ CK²F and b ≤ CK²O. This closes only the diagonal moment checkpoint.
actions.tool: Positive coefficient bound; factorial bound; diagonal entries controlled by the matrix norms.
actions.observation: Balancing variance and largest coefficient reproduces the two scales without a signed tail.

actions.title: Prepare scalar linear-form moments.
actions.summary: Use the independent subgaussian toolkit for deterministic linear coefficients.
actions.math: For deterministic v and p ≥ 2, ‖⟨v,X⟩‖p ≤ CK√p ‖v‖₂.
actions.check: Mean zero, independence and the scalar ψ₂ bounds imply subgaussian control of each fixed linear form. Conditional use requires coefficients independent of the coordinates being averaged.
actions.tool: Independent centered subgaussian linear-form bound and subgaussian moment characterization.
actions.observation: After separating the coordinate sets, one side can act as fixed coefficients.

actions.title: Decouple cross terms with Bernoulli selectors.
actions.summary: Average over random coordinate partitions and use convexity of the absolute pth power.
actions.math:
δᵢ independent Bernoulli(1/2), independent of X.
Sδ = Σᵢ≠ⱼ δᵢ(1 − δⱼ)aᵢⱼXᵢXⱼ; 𝔼δSδ = S/4.
‖S‖p ≤ 4(𝔼δ𝔼X|Sδ|ᵖ)¹ᐟᵖ.
For fixed Λ = {i: δᵢ = 1}, Sδ = XΛᵀ B XΛᶜ, B = AΛ,Λᶜ.
actions.check: The disjoint coordinate subvectors are independent. The identity is valid for nonsymmetric A as well. Empty blocks contribute zero.
actions.observation: The selectors trade dependent cross terms for bilinear forms on independent coordinate sets.

actions.title: Reduce the off-diagonal goal to a vector norm.
actions.summary: Condition on the second coordinate block and apply the linear-form moment estimate.
actions.math:
For fixed Λ, Y = XΛᶜ:
‖Sδ‖p ≤ CK√p (𝔼‖BY‖₂ᵖ)¹ᐟᵖ.
It suffices to show ‖BY‖Lp(ℓ₂) ≤ CK(‖B‖F + √p‖B‖).
Then average over δ and use ‖B‖F ≤ F, ‖B‖ ≤ O.
actions.check: The conditional scalar inequality is available, but the vector bound is still an obligation. Uniform block bounds are required before averaging over δ.
actions.tool: Conditional linear-form moment bound; coordinate projections.
actions.observation: A second naive √p factor would lose the desired √p F term; vector norm control matters.

actions.title: Read the vector norm through a Gaussian projection.
actions.summary: Reduce the vector checkpoint to a Gaussian norm estimate; the projection normalization cancels a √p factor.
actions.math:
g standard Gaussian in the row space of B, independent of Y; ap = ‖g₁‖p ≍ √p.
ap ‖BY‖Lp(ℓ₂) = ‖⟨g,BY⟩‖Lp(g,Y)
≤ CK√p ‖Bᵀg‖Lp(ℓ₂).
It suffices to bound ‖Bᵀg‖Lp(ℓ₂) ≤ ‖B‖F + C√p‖B‖.
actions.check: Condition on Y for the exact Gaussian projection identity, then on g for the subgaussian linear-form inequality. Divide by ap ≥ c√p; the Gaussian norm estimate remains unproved here.
actions.tool: Gaussian projection identity and scalar Gaussian moments; conditional linear-form bound.
actions.observation: Random projection preserves the Euclidean norm in Lp up to an explicit scalar factor.

actions.title: Apply Gaussian Lipschitz concentration.
actions.summary: Establish the explicit additional toolkit dependency of the alternative proof.
actions.math:
f(g) = ‖Bᵀg‖₂ is ‖B‖-Lipschitz.
‖f − 𝔼f‖p ≤ C√p ‖B‖; 𝔼f ≤ (𝔼f²)¹ᐟ² = ‖B‖F.
Hence ‖Bᵀg‖Lp(ℓ₂) ≤ ‖B‖F + C√p ‖B‖.
actions.check: g is a standard Gaussian vector. Triangle inequality proves the Lipschitz constant; Jensen and the Gaussian covariance compute the mean bound. The toolkit statement is independent of Hanson–Wright.
actions.tool: HDP-2: Theorem 5.2.3 (Gaussian concentration), Proposition 2.6.1 (subgaussian moments); Jensen and Minkowski.
actions.observation: Gaussian norm concentration keeps the Frobenius scale in the mean and the operator scale in fluctuations.

actions.title: Close the subgaussian vector moment checkpoint.
actions.summary: Insert Gaussian norm control into the projection reduction.
actions.math:
ap ‖BY‖Lp(ℓ₂) ≤ CK√p (‖B‖F + C√p‖B‖).
ap ≥ c√p gives ‖BY‖Lp(ℓ₂) ≤ CK(‖B‖F + √p‖B‖).
actions.check: The √p factors outside the parentheses cancel. This does not yet prove the scalar off-diagonal estimate; substitute it back into the conditional inequality next.
actions.tool: Established projection inequality, Gaussian norm bound, and ap ≍ √p.
actions.observation: Have and want meet at the vector norm checkpoint.

actions.title: Close the off-diagonal moment checkpoint.
actions.summary: Return through conditioning and the selector average to the original cross terms.
actions.math:
For every Λ, ‖Sδ‖p ≤ CK²(√p‖B‖F + p‖B‖) ≤ CK²(√p F + p O).
‖S‖p ≤ 4(𝔼δ𝔼|Sδ|ᵖ)¹ᐟᵖ ≤ CK²(√p F + p O).
actions.check: B is a row/column projection of A, so both block norms are bounded uniformly. Absorb 4 into the universal constant.
actions.tool: Established selector, conditional, and vector moment inequalities.
actions.observation: The desired two matrix scales survive decoupling and averaging.

actions.title: The absolute-moment estimate meets the main goal.
actions.summary: Assemble the two moment branches. This is the main meeting of the forward and backward proof layers.
actions.math:
For every even p ≥ 2:
‖Q‖p ≤ ‖D‖p + ‖S‖p ≤ C₀K²(√p F + p O).
actions.check: Both branches have been established under the same hypotheses and for all even p ≥ 2. The tail theorem still requires choosing p and checking the small-threshold regime.
actions.tool: Minkowski; the two established moment bounds.
actions.observation: The whole-form estimate closes a local goal, not yet the final tail theorem.

actions.title: Choose an even moment and apply absolute Markov.
actions.summary: At large q, a moment order proportional to q gives exponential decay directly for |Q|.
actions.math:
q = min{t²/(K⁴F²), t/(K²O)}. Choose α > 0 with C₀(√α + α) ≤ 1/e.
If αq ≥ 4, p = 2⌊αq/2⌋ has αq/2 ≤ p ≤ αq and p ≥ 2.
‖Q‖p/t ≤ 1/e. Therefore ℙ(|Q| ≥ t) ≤ (‖Q‖p/t)ᵖ ≤ e⁻ᵖ ≤ e^(−αq/2).
actions.check: Even rounding stays in the proved moment domain. q ≤ t²/(K⁴F²) and q ≤ t/(K²O) control the two terms separately. This result covers only αq ≥ 4.
actions.tool: Markov on |Q|ᵖ; the assembled moment estimate; even-integer parameter choice.
actions.observation: The finite optimal moment order captures both tail regimes at once.

actions.title: Handle small thresholds and close Hanson–Wright.
actions.summary: Combine the large-q estimate with the trivial probability bound, and include degenerate cases.
actions.math:
Take 0 < c ≤ α log(2)/4.
If αq < 4, 2e^(−cq) ≥ 1 ≥ ℙ(|Q| ≥ t).
If αq ≥ 4, e^(−αq/2) ≤ 2e^(−cq).
Thus ℙ(|Q| ≥ t) ≤ 2 exp[−c min{t²/(K⁴F²), t/(K²O)}].
actions.check: At t = 0 use probability ≤ 1. If A = 0 or K = 0, Q = 0 almost surely and every positive-threshold probability vanishes. All introduced goals are now discharged; the excluded sign/upper-tail strategy never appears.
actions.tool: Probability ≤ 1; elementary constants and zero cases.
actions.observation: The alternative reaches the same final theorem without rejoining the upper-tail checkpoint.
